page: Microsoft Azure E48ds_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EDSv4 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C x86_64 processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The processor includes a 35 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and cryptography acceleration via AES and SHA-NI. The instance is equipped with 384.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Additionally, it includes 1843 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not bundle any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPU hardware.

Benchmark data indicates balanced performance characteristics across most workloads. The server demonstrates strong memory bandwidth, achieving 230.36 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 111.32 GB/sec for large-block write operations, both placing in the top 25% of tested configurations. CPU-bound tasks, such as stress-ng multi-core (44703.83) and Geekbench multi-core (13298.0), perform in the average tier. However, single-threaded decompression tasks show limitations, with bzip3 single-threaded decompression scoring in the bottom 25% at 8.76 GB/sec. Similarly, large-scale LLM inference tasks represent a performance tradeoff, with text generation speeds for both small and medium models falling into the weak category.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E48ds_v4 offers high memory density and local storage capacity relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads without the overhead of specialized GPU hardware. The combination of 384.0 GB of RAM, dedicated Intel Xeon cores, and 1843 GB of local storage makes this instance well-suited for relational database management systems, in-memory caching layers like Redis, and enterprise-level data processing applications. It is also highly applicable for static web serving and multi-threaded file compression tasks.
